- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >3x from prior day), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., cap at 2x prior peak).
- Forecasts with high volatility in sentiment history (alternating +/–0.33) show poor persistence; use moving average of last 5–7 days to anchor short-term forecasts.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early forecast days (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — if history shows consolidation, forecast should be closer to recent mean, not extreme.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.67, reduce forecast by 5–15%; if sentiment <0.33, increase by 5–15%.
- Avoid forecasting spikes >2x the 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) — otherwise, cap at 1.5x to prevent overcorrection.
